title: A runner that talks about the spend limit is not a runner that hit it
goal: The loop decides whether it has stalled by reading the words its own runner printed. So a runner that finishes a piece of work about the spend limit, or a digest that reports last week stall, gets recorded as having hit the limit itself: the loop marks itself unhealthy, backs off, and the dashboard says the build has stopped when it has not. Make the loop tell a real refusal from a runner talking about one, so the health it reports is the health it has.
acceptance: A runner whose own output mentions the spend limit, or a sign-in, while finishing its work normally is recorded as ok, not as an environment failure
A real refusal from the CLI is still caught exactly as it is today, for both a task run and a digest run
The 2026-09-12 digest run in queue/history.jsonl is replayed against the fixed check and comes out ok
The reproduction in the notes becomes a test that fails on today code and passes after the fix
anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task

log.note: adversarial review before building: the tempting fix is to tighten the phrases (require "hit your ... spend limit"), and it is the wrong one. It trades recall for precision and the next wording the CLI ships walks straight past it, while a runner quoting THAT wording still trips it. The thing that actually separates the two cases is not the sentence, it is who wrote the line, so the rule is about channel and shape. Second finding: fixing pickRunnerError alone is not enough, because recordRunnerExit re-reads the single line it returns and reaches its own verdict, and by then the tool calls that prove the runner worked are gone. The verdict has to be made once, where the whole run is visible, and carried.

test first: scenario 5 added to queue/bin/failure-drill.sh, running the REAL go loop with a fake CLI that quotes the refusal in a tool call, in its prose and in its result summary while finishing its work normally. On the unfixed code it failed exactly as reported: 1 runner_failed event with outcome spend, the digest deferred, and the loop window printing "spend limit hit: the agent refused to run ... raise the limit". Scenarios 1 to 4 passed throughout.

built: queue-lib.mjs gains classifyRunnerOutput(stderr, stdout) -> { line, reason }, the one place the verdict is reached. stderr is the CLI's own channel so a refusal there is a refusal; stdout only carries one when the runner never got to work, since a single tool-call line means the CLI let it run. environmentSignature now refuses any line the loop's own formatter wrote (the tool marker, the result banner, the session line) whatever it says, which alone makes the recorded 2026-09-12 error replay as ok. recordRunnerExit takes reason as an INPUT and no longer re-sniffs when it is given. queue.mjs: new runner-classify command printing RUNNER_ERR/RUNNER_REASON as shell assignments (single-quoted, apostrophes escaped), and runner-exit takes --reason. go-loop.sh: run_runner evals runner-classify, record_exit passes --reason through. stream-format.mjs carries a comment saying its marker is load-bearing.

verified: failure-drill.sh all five scenarios pass (scenario 3 still proves a real spend refusal fails a digest run from the first refusal, scenario 2 the same for sign-in, scenario 1 the per-task parking rule). The real 2026-09-12 entry, read out of queue/history.jsonl rather than retyped, replays as outcome ok health ok. A real refusal driven through the CLI the loop actually calls still gives OUTCOME=spend REASON=spend HEALTH=unhealthy ENVFAIL=1. churn, decision, state-poll, audit-index and manager-due drills pass. Scripts/test.sh: 6376 tests in 516 suites passed.

acceptance: (1) covered by scenario 5 end to end, plus the direct checks for a refusal quoted in a tool call, in a summary and in a sign-in phrasing. (2) covered by scenarios 1, 2 and 3 unchanged, plus scenario 5's checks on both channels. (3) the recorded 2026-09-12 digest run replays as ok, read from the real history.jsonl. (4) the reproduction is scenario 5 and failed on the unfixed code before passing on the fixed one. (5) rough edges are in the audit rather than filed as tasks, since none of them is a defect: see the note below.

left rough, deliberately not filed: the notes' reproduction transcribes the tool marker as a plain ">", and in that ASCII form on three lines it is genuinely indistinguishable from a refusal and still reads as one. The real stream never looks like that. A mid-work refusal reaching only the formatted stream would now be recorded as a plain failure rather than named, but every one on record reached the error channel too and a task run counts the failure either way, so the loss is wording, not reaction. Filing either as a task would take a p2 slot off the focus for something that is not broken; both are written into queue/audits/2026-09-13-loop-refusal-detection.json where the user can disagree line by line.
noted on the related task a-loop-stalled-on-the-spend-limit-reaches-the-pe that this landed first, as its notes asked: that notification can now trust status.lastError.reason.

The loop no longer reads its own runner's words as a refusal. classifyRunnerOutput reaches the verdict once with the whole run in view (stderr = the CLI's own channel, so a refusal there is real; stdout only when the runner never got to work, since one tool call means the CLI let it run) and recordRunnerExit is told rather than re-sniffing. Verified: failure-drill.sh scenario 5 failed on the old code and passes now, scenarios 1-4 still green so real refusals are caught as before, the recorded 2026-09-12 digest run replays from history.jsonl as ok, and a real refusal through the CLI the loop calls still gives OUTCOME=spend HEALTH=unhealthy. Scripts/test.sh green. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-13-loop-refusal-detection.json. Commit f51cd327, pushed.
